title: Design System Manager - Consultant.e
description: Mindset Chez Thiga, nous considérons qu’un Design System n’est pas seulement un ensemble de composants ou de règles : c’est un produit à part entière . Un produit pensé pour évoluer, répondre aux besoins des équipes, et accompagner la croissance de l’entreprise. Créer et faire vivre un Design System demande une vision , une stratégie claire , et une gouvernance solide . Il faut piloter son adoption, anticiper ses usages à grande échelle, et s’assurer qu’il réponde aux enjeux à la fois du Design et de la Tech. C’est un levier puissant pour faire monter en maturité les organisations, structurer la collaboration entre les équipes, et diffuser une culture produit forte. Aujourd'hui, un Design System bien structuré est aussi la condition sine qua non pour tirer pleinement parti de l'IA dans les workflows design et prototypage. Tokens cohérents, composants documentés, nomenclature rigoureuse autant de fondations qui permettent d'exploiter les outils d'IA générative (Figma Make, Lovable, v0...) de manière fiable et scalable. Le.la Design System Manager de demain est celui.celle qui anticipe ces usages et structure son système en conséquence. Les Design System Managers que nous recherchons pensent leur système comme un produit vivant, automatisé au maximum, et conçu pour connecter Design et Ingénierie dans un workflow sans friction . How we work together 🤝 Mettre en place des rituels d'adoption et d'amélioration continue :offices hours, sessions de feedback, contribution guidelines pour que le DS soit co-construit et adopté par toutes les équipes. Aligner Design et Engineering en continu : organiser des syncs réguliers avec les équipes dev pour garantir la cohérence entre les composants Figma et leur implémentation code. Le DS ne vit pas dans Figma seul; il vit dans la production. Piloter l'alignement stratégique multi-équipes : s'assurer que Produit, Tech, Design et business partagent la même vision et roadmap du DS, intégrée au même niveau que les autres produits. Répondre aux besoins des utilisateurs et contributeurs : centraliser les demandes, prioriser les évolutions, et faciliter la contribution fluide de designers, développeurs et PMs. Fédérer autour d'une culture DS partagée : faire du DS un produit vivant et co-créé, en favorisant des échanges transparents et en embarquant les équipes dans sa vision long terme How we get work done 🚀 Définir et piloter la roadmap du DS : feuille de route alignée sur les priorités produit et business, avec des objectifs mesurables à court et long terme. Automatiser les workflows du DS au maximum : pipelines de tokens, synchronisation design to code en temps réel, scripts de génération de documentation, réduire au minimum les tâches manuelles et les risques de désynchronisation. Structurer le DS pour l'IA et le prototypage rapide : concevoir une architecture de composants et de tokens qui rende le DS exploitable par les outils d'IA générative (Figma Make, Cursor, v0, Lovable...). Cela implique : nomenclature stricte,variantes bien définies, props documentées, et une logique de composants qui s'aligne avec les patterns du code. Garantir la cohérence design-code : mettre en place des outils de vérification automatique pour s'assurer que ce qui est designé est bien ce qui est développé sans avoir à le vérifier manuellement. Promouvoir les bonnes pratiques à grande échelle : formations, ateliers, documentation vivante pour que le DS soit utilisé de manière fluide et scalable par toutes les équipes. Mesurer l'impact et itérer : KPIs d'adoption, indicateurs de qualité, retours qualitatifs pour évaluer l'impact du DS et ajuster les priorités How our work creates impact 🎯   Accélérer le delivery produit : composants prêts à l'emploi, pipelines automatisés et prompts IA calibrés sur le DS. Les équipes conçoivent et développent plus vite, avec moins de friction Rendre le prototypage IA fiable et scalable : un DS bien structuré devient le langage commun entre les designers et les outils d'IA les prototypes générés sont cohérents avec la prod, pas jetables Garantir la qualité et la cohérence design à l'échelle : expérience utilisateur homogène, identité de marque renforcée, dette design et technique réduite Réduire la dette et simplifier la maintenance : moins de doublons, moins de variantes inutiles, un code plus accessible et plus performant Faire monter l'organisation en maturité design : culture de collaboration Design × Tech structurée, vision stratégique du design renforcée, documentation vivante comme levier de montée en compétence Compétences 💼 Vision système et stratégie DS : u sais définir une stratégie de DS et la décliner en roadmap concrète, en alignement avec les priorités produit, tech et business. Tu fais preuve de leadership pour porter cette vision et embarquer les équipes. Alignement Design-Engineering :  tu as une solide compréhension des enjeux front-end (tokens, design-to-code, systèmes de composants) et tu dialogues en égal avec les développeurs pas seulement pour les convaincre, mais pour co-construire les bonnes solutions. Automatisation et tooling DS : tu maîtrises les pipelines de tokens, les outils de documentation (Storybook, Zeroheight) et tu as une appétence pour l'automatisation des workflows DS. IA et prototypage avancé : tu comprends comment un DS structuré permet de tirer parti des outils d'IA générative pour le design et le prototypage. Tu anticipes ces usages dans les décisions d'architecture du DS. Gestion de produit interne : tu pilotes le DS comme un vrai produit : besoins utilisateurs, priorisation, KPIs, itération continue. Communication et influence : tu sais formuler des livrables synthétiques et stratégiques (vision, roadmap, modèles de gouvernance, dashboards) pour aligner des interlocuteurs variés équipes opérationnelles, direction produit, stakeholders. Outils : figma (Variables, Dev Mode, Make), Storybook, Zeroheight, Notion, Jira/Linear, Style Dictionary, et une bonne aisance avec les environnements no-code/low-code et outils IA de prototypage. Anglais courant : à l'écrit comme à l'oral Qualités 🌟   Tu penses en systèmes : tu comprends les logiques systémiques et sais structurer un DS cohérent, extensible, et exploitable par l'IA Tu automatises par réflexe : tu cherches à réduire les tâches manuelles et à construire des workflows robustes qui s'auto-maintiennent. Tu es le pont entre Design et Tech : tu parles les deux langages et tu sais créer les conditions d'un alignement durable entre les équipes. Tu portes une vision : tu es capable de convaincre, d'aligner et d'embarquer des designers comme des ingénieurs, des opérationnels comme des dirigeants. Tu pilotes ton DS comme un produit : besoins utilisateurs internes, KPIs, roadmap priorisée tu traites le DS avec la même rigueur qu'un produit client. Tu restes curieux·se et en veille : sur les outils, les pratiques et l'évolution rapide des Design Systems et des usages IA dans le design Expérience 📇 Tu as au moins 5 ans d'expérience en Product Design, Design System Management ou un rôle similaire, avec une trajectoire confirmée ou senior Tu as déjà créé ou fortement structuré un Design System de zéro ou à grande échelle , pas seulement contribué à l'un Tu as mis en place des pipelines de tokens, des processus d'automatisation et des intégrations design to code Tu as expérimenté avec des outils d'IA générative , dans un contexte design ou DS (Figma Make, Cursor, v0, Lovable, ou équivalent) Tu as travaillé aussi bien en scale-up qu'en grand groupe, ce qui te donne une bonne lecture des modèles d'organisation et des leviers pour faire évoluer la maturité design. Tu as travaillé en méthodologie agile et sais comment intégrer le DS dans ces processus de delivery. Ce que nous offrons 🎊 Un on-boarding pour rencontrer tes collègues  De l’apprentissage avec minimum 5 jours de formations à l’année, des sessions de partage hebdomadaires et du contenu pour te faire monter en compétences Du mentoring sur ta mission par un pair plus confirmé  Du confort avec deux jours de télétravail par semaine (selon ton client) complétés par un accès à un catalogue de matériels, ainsi qu’un Macbook Air ou un PC selon ta préférence. Du fun avec des Thigapéros, des Team building et un séminaire (en prêtant attention à notre empreinte carbone). Et pleins d’autres avantages comme une carte Swile, le remboursement de ton abonnement de transport à 50%/forfait mobilité durable, etc. Les étapes du process 🎢 Un pré-entretien téléphonique avec une membre de l’équipe Recrutement L'évaluation de ton portfolio par nos Designers Une rencontre avec un.e Principal, un.e Manager de la Tribe ou un Partner pour s’assurer que nous partageons les mêmes valeurs et ambitions Un entretien plus opérationnel avec un ou deux membres senior de notre équipe pour évaluer ta compréhension du rôle de Design System Manager, ta capacité à résoudre des problèmes liés au Design System, tes convictions, tes attentes, etc. Une dernière rencontre pour finaliser le process, s’accorder sur une ambition commune, des objectifs et un périmètre d’intervention 🤝 Thiga accueille toutes les personnes compétentes et passionnées et s'engage en faveur de la diversité culturelle, l'égalité de genre et l'emploi des travailleurs handicapés — au contraire nous considérons la diversité comme une grande richesse ! title: Product Frontend Engineer
description: quinn is becoming the way people employ, across the globe, through one app. quinn is an app-based, managed payroll and employment-administration service. We run it for private households employing a cleaner, nanny, or caretaker, and for businesses that manage employment relationships at scale. The customer stays the legal employer: quinn registers the employment, runs payroll, and handles social insurance, taxes, and filings on their behalf, automated end to end. Where everyone else sells software, quinn sells the outcome. We don't sell payroll software. We run payroll. The purpose behind it is simple: Fair employment. For all. Correct and fair employment, made simple and accessible for any employer and any employee, in any market quinn enters. Where this is going Think about what Revolut did to banking. All of the complexity (the regulation, the clearing, the compliance) handled invisibly in the background, and one simple experience at the front. Nobody using Revolut thinks about what happens behind the screen when they open a new account, swap currencies or send money abroad. It just works, in a couple of taps. Nobody should have to think about it in order to employ someone either. That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience. One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy. Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled. Why this role exists Today , quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with. What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards. That is the opening. How we work We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing. We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way. And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high. Tasks What you will own Everything on the screen: The frontend of the quinn app and the web app. App first. One app for everyone who uses quinn: the employer, the employee, and our own support team working inside the customer's account. The frontend of Maestro, our internal batch tool. Desktop and dense: queues, runs, tables, filters, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts. A different discipline from the app, built on the same components. The component library across quinn Home and quinn Business: one frontend, one experience, every market and every device. Whether the app feels native: response, scrolling, gestures, transitions, biometric login, push. Nothing that gives away it isn't native. The quality of what you ship. Nothing leaves your hands half-finished. Where design ends, engineering begins. We have a design team, and they own how quinn looks and behaves: the flows, the visual design, the tokens, the component specs. You don't design. You own everything from there: how it is built, and everything a design file cannot reasonably specify, such as gestures, keyboard, safe areas, what happens between the drawn breakpoints, the loading, offline, pending and failed states, what a three-line German label does to a layout that was designed for English. You are in the room before design starts, saying what already exists in the library and what a new pattern costs. Not at the end, receiving a handover. When you and design disagree, they decide how it looks and behaves and you decide how it is built. Nothing enters the component library without both of you. Requirements Who we are looking for You care about interfaces more than anyone else in the room. You see the two-pixel misalignment without being told, and it bothers you until it is fixed. You build and maintain UI components and design systems, not one-off screens. You can build a mobile app that feels like one. And you can also build a desktop tool full of tables, filters and keyboard shortcuts, because Maestro is one. You understand UX and how people actually behave, not only how a screen looks. And you write code other people can take over: scalable, structured, documented. Not something that only works while you are in the building. You are independent and decisive. Nobody will spec every detail for you and nobody will review your pixels. You are fluent in English, no other language is required. And if you have a portfolio, a live product, or anything you have shipped that you are proud of, show it to us. Not a requirement, but it tells us more than a CV does. Most importantly: you want this one. Not a frontend role at a company where the frontend is a chore. This one, the app nobody has built yet, the standard nobody has set yet, and a company where getting it right actually decides whether the strategy works. The Team We are a small, fast, direct team. We do not have a lot of process or a lot of hierarchy. We do have a clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we actually mean: Be open, Own it, Speak up, Keep it simple, Bias for action. This is one of the most important hires we will make this year. We are not rushing it and we are not filling a seat. We are looking for the person who reads this and thinks: finally. We have a design team, and they own how quinn looks and behaves: the flows, the visual design, the tokens, the component specs. You don't design. You own everything from there: how it is built, and everything a design file cannot reasonably specify, such as gestures, keyboard, safe areas, what happens between the drawn breakpoints, the loading, offline, pending and failed states, what a three-line German label does to a layout that was designed for English. You are in the room before design starts, saying what already exists in the library and what a new pattern costs. Not at the end, receiving a handover. When you and design disagree, they decide how it looks and behaves and you decide how it is built. Nothing enters the component library without both of you.

Requirements

Who we are looking for

You care about interfaces more than anyone else in the room. You see the two-pixel misalignment without being told, and it bothers you until it is fixed.

You build and maintain UI components and design systems, not one-off screens. You can build a mobile app that feels like one. And you can also build a desktop tool full of tables, filters and keyboard shortcuts, because Maestro is one. You understand UX and how people actually behave, not only how a screen looks. And you write code other people can take over: scalable, structured, documented. Not something that only works while you are in the building.

You are independent and decisive. Nobody will spec every detail for you and nobody will review your pixels.

You are fluent in English, no other language is required. And if you have a portfolio, a live product, or anything you have shipped that you are proud of, show it to us. Not a requirement, but it tells us more than a CV does.

Most importantly: you want this one. Not a frontend role at a company where the frontend is a chore. This one, the app nobody has built yet, the standard nobody has set yet, and a company where getting it right actually decides whether the strategy works.

The Team

We are a small, fast, direct team. We do not have a lot of process or a lot of hierarchy. We do have a clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we actually mean: Be open, Own it, Speak up, Keep it simple, Bias for action.

This is one of the most important hires we will make this year. We are not rushing it and we are not filling a seat. We are looking for the person who reads this and thinks: finally.

Parkview Invest AG ist eine inhabergeführte Schweizer Investmentgesellschaft mit einem diversifizierten Portfolio aus privaten Unternehmensbeteiligungen, Immobilien, Fonds und weiteren Vermögenswerten.

Unsere Aktivitäten umfassen mehrere Gesellschaften und Beteiligungen im In- und Ausland. Im Rahmen der strategischen Weiterentwicklung konzentrieren wir uns verstärkt auf die professionelle Verwaltung bestehender Investments, die Vereinfachung unserer Unternehmensstrukturen und die effiziente Steuerung unserer Finanz- und Administrationsprozesse.

title: Mechanical Forward Deployed Engineer - Switzerland
description: <h3><strong>About CoLab</strong></h3> <p>At CoLab, we help mechanical engineering teams bring life-changing products to market years sooner.</p> <p>We build AI for engineers designing cars, medical devices, and jet engines. Products this complex aren't sketched and sent to production. Teams spend months on iterations, reviews, and tests, predicting how every part performs before anything is built. CoLab is where those reviews happen, and we capture the rationale behind every change. Other tools show what changed between versions. Only CoLab knows why. That's how our AI helps manufacturers like Bobcat, Triumph Motorcycles, and GE Appliances make better decisions, eliminate rework cycles, and get to market faster.</p> <p>Proudly based in St. John’s, Newfoundland, CoLab started with one customer in 2018. Since then we’ve raised a<a href="https://financialpost.com/pmn/business-wire-news-releases-pmn/ai-is-changing-engineering-colab-just-raised-72m-to-lead-the-transformation"> $72M Series C</a>, been named the 57th fastest growing company in North America by Deloitte (<a href="https://financialpost.com/pmn/business-wire-news-releases-pmn/colab-ranked-number-57-fastest-growing-company-in-north-america-on-the-2025-deloitte-technology-fast-500">Fast 500™</a>), signed multi-year<a href="https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-bombardier-signs-contract-colab-ai-software/"> AI partnerships with companies like Bombardier</a>, and grown to a team of 250+.</p> <h3><strong>About the Role</strong></h3> <p>This is a high-impact role that helps define how CoLab delivers technical value to its most strategic customers in Aerospace and Defence. CoLab is a category-creating product, which means adoption isn't just a rollout. It's a change in how the organization works.</p> <p>In this role, you'd act as a trusted advisor, leveraging people, process, and technology to help teams rethink how they manage feedback, data, and decision-making across design and PLM. That means getting deep into customer workflows, testing new ways of working, and building repeatable methods the rest of the team can scale.</p> <p>You'll work alongside a Customer Success Manager, and use what you learn on the front line to help shape product direction. This role isn't about selling or pitching. It's about deeply understanding engineering problems and solving them alongside the customer.</p> <p>We are looking for a candidate in Switzerland to work regularly on-site with local CoLab customers.</p> <h2>Our Ideal Candidate</h2> <p>You’re a mechanical engineer by trade and have worked as a designer in an A&amp;D company. You also understand the full product development life cycle: how design, manufacturing, quality, and engineering leadership depend on each other, and where collaboration breaks down. You can coach those teams toward working together better.</p> <p>You know how to improve that life cycle with technology. Maybe you’ve championed internal tools or created automation or scripts.</p> <p>You also know a process that makes sense on paper won’t get adopted on its own. You can meet people where they are, including the stakeholders who don’t want to change.</p> <p>You don’t need to be the loudest voice in the room, but you can run a sprint and lead a cross-functional project. If the average person might find this job too undefined or complex, that probably excites you.</p> <h2>Job Responsibilities</h2> <ul> <li>Mapping a customer's current-state design review and engineering workflows, and defining the target-state process their teams will actually adopt.</li> <li>Deploying and tuning CoLab's AI capabilities against a customer's own standards, drawing checklists, and design guidelines, and diagnosing what's working and what isn't.</li> <li>Providing mechanical engineering expertise to validate AI-generated results and ensure engineering rigor.</li> <li>Investigating and solving complex engineering data and integration challenges across PLM, ERP, QMS, and traditional design feedback tools.</li> <li>Expanding adoption into new teams, programs, and sites within the account, partnering with the Customer Success Manager on where the next opportunity sits.</li> <li>Collaborating with product teams to identify feature gaps, improve capabilities, and refine AutoReview.</li> </ul> <h2>Qualifications</h2> <p><strong>Must-haves:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Background in mechanical design engineering, ideally in a medium- to large-sized organization.</li> <li>Strong understanding of PLM &amp; ERP systems and enterprise engineering data architecture.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to lead technical projects and cross-functional collaborations.</li> <li>Experience working directly with customers or internal stakeholders to solve technical problems.</li> <li>Comfort working in fast-changing, ambiguous environments.</li> <li>Strong written communication and documentation skills.</li> <li>Working knowledge of high-level AI architecture, specifically LLMs.</li> <li>Familiarity with APIs, data integrations, and enterprise architecture concepts.</li> <li>Located in Switzerland&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>Nice-to-haves:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience with internal tool development, scripting, or automation.</li> <li>Exposure to AI/ML tools applied to engineering workflows.</li> <li>Prior work in design consulting or product development at scale.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Travel Expectations</strong></h2> <p>While this is a fully remote role, travel is a consistent part of the job. There are two primary types of travel you can expect:</p> <ul> <li><strong>Team Weeks:</strong> Once per quarter, the sales team or entire company gets together in person. These typically involve traveling out on a Monday and returning on a Thursday or Friday. Two of these each year are held at our headquarters in St. John's, Newfoundland, Canada and the others take place in more central locations that evolve as the team grows.</li> <li><strong>On-sites:</strong> This role will work closely with a local customer with expectations to be on site with that customer, so there will likely be far less travel than our typical MFDE roll. That being said, in the event the local customer were to no longer work with us, the following is our standard MFDE travel expectations: “For most of our large deployment customers, we will visit on-site during kick-off and key expansion opportunities. Most on-sites involve 2-3 days with the customer, with travel on either side. Travel is primarily within North America, and you can expect 4 customer on-sites per quarter.”</li> </ul> <h2>Extra Details</h2> <ul> <li>This is a full-time, permanent position with a competitive compensation package that includes stock options.</li> <li>Unlimited paid vacation and extended health benefits&nbsp;</li> </ul> <h2>Equity Note</h2> <p>Frequently cited statistics show that people who identify with historically marginalized groups are likely to apply to jobs only if they meet 100% of the qualifications. We encourage you to help us break that statistic and apply even if you don't meet every single qualification. Your potential is what matters most to us.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

raw.title: IoT Embedded Systems Engineer
raw.description:
• Take ownership of the development of IoT systems, with a focus on embedded software, system architecture, and hardware and firmware integration

  • Design and develop robust, efficient, and scalable embedded software for IoT products based on microcontroller platforms and, optionally, Linux based systems

  • Provide technical guidance for hardware development in collaboration with external partners, including reviewing and challenging PCB designs to ensure functionality, quality, and manufacturability

  • Collaborate closely with mechanical, software, and cloud engineering teams to ensure seamless end to end system integration

  • Define and refine product requirements from initial concept through to mass production in collaboration with internal and external stakeholders

  • Develop and integrate prototypes and support the transition from development into serial production together with manufacturing partners

  • Contribute to the continuous evolution of the embedded platform, including MCU based solutions as well as optional Linux and Yocto based components

  • Develop pragmatic testing strategies to ensure the functionality, reliability, and quality of both hardware and firmware

  • Support development and manufacturing partners with debugging, technical documentation, and production ramp up

  • Provide Level 3 technical support for complex system, firmware, and hardware related issues

  • Travel approximately 5 to 10 percent to support development partners, product validation activities, and product launches


  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Embedded Systems, Computer Science, or a related discipline, or equivalent practical experience

  • Several years of hands on experience in embedded development, including firmware development and hardware related engineering

  • Strong understanding of hardware design and PCB layouts, with the ability to review design decisions and collaborate effectively with hardware development teams

  • Strong expertise in embedded firmware development and software architecture for microcontroller platforms such as ARM Cortex, ESP32, or STM32

  • Experience with sensor integration and wireless communication technologies such as BLE and WiFi

  • Experience with embedded Linux systems, particularly Yocto, is an advantage, especially in environments combining System on Modules with MCU based architectures

  • Broad system level understanding of mechanics, sensors, actuators, and their integration into robust IoT products

  • Hands on experience with hardware testing, debugging tools, and automated production testing

  • Familiarity with certification standards such as CE and FCC is an advantage

  • Fluent in German and English, with additional languages considered a plus

title: Product Manager - Surveying & Mapping Drone
description: Join the Wingtra team and become part of this venture-backed robotics scaleup with a global and international team of 125+ dedicated Wingtranauts who want to see their actions have a positive and lasting impact on the world. Founded more than 8 years ago at ETH Zurich, Europe’s leading robotics university, our goal is to build the best aerial robots to digitize the world at the push of a button and set the basis for faster and better decisions. Wingtra provides efficient and reliable data solutions to a variety of industries ranging from mining, construction and agriculture to humanitarian organizations, environmentalists and wildlife monitoring groups. We are reaching for the stars and together we might just get there. Open communication, asking hard questions and valuing diverse viewpoints are but a few things that will help us achieve our goals. Above all we will never stop learning and striving to help each other reach our maximum potential. Now we need someone to help decide what we build next. You’ll own the priorities for our data capture platform, from the aircraft to the sensors they carry. You’ll work side by side with customers in the field, Wingtra engineers and Wingtranauts across all business functions. Your job is to find the problems that matter most to our customers and turn good ideas into products people love. Inside Wingtra you’re the voice of the user. Outside you’re the voice of the product. Responsibilities Know your customers. You spend time with survey and mapping teams in the field. You learn how they work, how they buy, what else they could use and what they still can’t do. Set the priorities. You weigh customer value, market opportunity, development effort, price and margin. Then you make a clear call on what comes next. Test ideas early. You try them with customers and engineers, learn fast and adjust. Shape the product development. You steer the capture platform: aircraft, sensors, workflows and data deliverables. You make the performance, reliability and usability trade-offs together with engineering. Take it to market. You launch with Product Marketing, Sales, Support and partners and explain why the product matters. After launch you stay close to field results and keep supporting the product through its lifecycle. Follow the outcomes. You track customer outcomes, usage and commercial results. You use what you learn to pick the next problem to solve with the team. Requirements You have a taste for great products and a relentless drive to understand what makes users love them. You make things happen. You act like an owner and hold yourself accountable to outcomes not output. You care primarily about happy customers and a successful business. You bring people with you. You listen closely, speak clearly and earn trust with customers and engineers, including when you disagree. You find a way forward. You are very comfortable with ambiguity. You work constructively with people and constraints, know when to push and when to adapt. You’ve spent 3+ years developing or deploying hardware products and their software workflows, with clear ownership of product, operational or commercial results. You have a technical background in engineering, geospatial or another technical field. You’re commercially fluent. You read a pricing model, channel margin or renewal term and see why the business cares. You’re fluent in English and happy to travel regularly to customers and partners in the US and Europe. Plus You’ve founded a relevant business of your own, led surveying or drone operations, or built products for geospatial customers. You have hands-on experience with photogrammetry, LiDAR or bringing a commercial robotics product to market. If you enjoy teamwork more than being the individual superhero, and if you thrive in a feedback-driven culture and an exciting, unconventional yet structured and progressive start-up environment, we would love to hear from you.   • ElevenCreative empowers creators and marketers to generate and edit speech, music, image, and video across 70+ languages.

  • ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

How we work

  • High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

  • Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

  • AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

  • Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

  • Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

  • Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

  • Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

  • Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

  • Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

About the role

We're looking for an experienced, driven Strategic Account Executive to drive ElevenLabs' growth across Switzerland's largest enterprises. Our ideal candidate has a well-established network and a proven track record of selling to C-level and senior decision-makers at major Swiss brands and is passionate about the transformative possibilities of AI voice technology.

In this role you'll act as a strategic partner and trusted advisor, enabling clients to leverage our industry-leading models and ElevenAgents — our end-to-end platform for building and deploying AI voice agents — to reimagine their customer experience, internal workflows, and monetization strategies.

In this role you will:

  • Build and manage a growing portfolio of strategic accounts across Switzerland to help ElevenLabs meet its revenue goals.

  • Identify new business opportunities where ElevenLabs' conversational AI capabilities, including ElevenAgents, can drive customer engagement, contact center automation, and operational efficiency for consumer and retail brands.

  • Lead consultative, multi-stakeholder sales cycles, building compelling business cases that translate AI voice technology into measurable business value for senior executives and economic buyers.

  • Develop and maintain a deep understanding of the conversational AI landscape, including customer use cases, competitive solutions, and emerging trends, particularly as they apply to Swiss consumer and retail organizations operating at scale.

  • Demonstrate expertise, or a strong willingness to learn, about conversational AI and how ElevenLabs' voice technology can unlock value across customer support, virtual agents, IVR modernization, and in-app assistants.

  • Develop and execute account strategies to expand ElevenLabs' presence within the Swiss consumer and retail sector, navigating complex procurement and organizational structures.

  • Partner closely with Customer Success, FDEs and Solutions Engineering to ensure smooth onboarding, deployment, and expansion of accounts.

  • Serve as a trusted advisor to clients, educating C-suite and senior operations leaders on emerging trends in generative AI, voice interfaces, and conversational agents.

Requirements

  • 7+ years of quota-carrying strategic sales experience in SaaS or technology, ideally with exposure to AI, generative AI, LLM-based products, or API-driven platforms.

  • Proven success closing deals and managing long, complex sales cycles with multiple stakeholders across business, IT, legal, and procurement.

  • Well-connected in the Swiss consumer and retail landscape, with an existing network of senior individuals and strong executive presence and ability to build relationships at the C-suite and board level.

  • Experience selling technical solutions to product and engineering leaders; ability to translate complex technology into business value.

  • Deep understanding of enterprise procurement and legal processes in Switzerland, with the ability to accelerate deal velocity within complex organizational structures.

  • Comfort operating in an early-stage, high-growth environment, including building new playbooks and iterating quickly.

  • Passion for voice and audio AI and how it can unlock transformative value for customers.

  • A hybrid of customer and product-driven mentality that prioritizes client satisfaction and scale.

  • Swiss German is the preferred default language for this role; fluency in both Swiss German and French is a strong plus given Switzerland's multilingual market. Strong English is also required for internal collaboration.

Location

This is an in-country role based in Zurich.

title: Senior Projectmanager
description: Jouw Missie bij CCS Geen dag is hetzelfde in deze rol. Samen met je collega’s zorg je ervoor dat wij succesvol onze softwareoplossingen bij klanten implementeren en dat onze klanten een excellente dienstverlening krijgen! Voor deze complexe systeemimplementaties en integratieprojecten zoeken we een zeer ervaren projectmanager. Je leert de verzekeringsbranche kennen en klanten helpen. Dat doe je niet alleen: je werkt samen met enthousiaste collega’s in een projectteam. Voordelen voor de sollicitant Als projectmanager krijg je veel verantwoordelijkheid, help je klanten en samen met je projectteam zet je mooie resultaten neer. Je kunt deels thuiswerken, deels op ons kantoor in Woerden en bij verschillende klanten in Nederland. Tijdelijk werken vanuit het buitenland kan ook dankzij onze workation-regeling (maximaal 30 dagen aaneengesloten per jaar). Bij ons draait het om klantgericht werken én werkplezier. Daarom is er volop ruimte voor ontspanning en plezier. Denk aan een levend tafelvoetbaltoernooi, pubquiz en een bier- & wijnproeverij. Ons actieve Fun-team zorgt elke maand weer voor iets leuks. En als je reislust nog niet is gestild met 25 vakantiedagen en een workation, dan kun je zelfs tot 20 extra verlofdagen bijkopen. Genoeg redenen om verder te lezen en te ontdekken of deze functie iets voor jou is, toch? Een voorbeeld van je werkdag Opstarten: Aan het begin van je werkdag heb je een dagstart met zowel collega’s als projectteamleden van de klant. Hierin bespreken jullie de voortgang, resultaten en eventuele hulpvragen. Na de dagstart: Allereerst neem je nog wat tijd met een van de consultants naar aanleiding van de dagstart. Je coacht en begeleidt de consultant en helpt deze met een hulpvraag. Vervolgens ga je aan de slag met het opstellen van de voortgangsrapportage. Hiermee zorg je voor proactieve en transparante rapportage over het project aan de klant. De stuurgroep met de klant is volgende week, vandaag spreek je samen met de delivery manager deze stuurgroep voor. Wat zijn de belangrijkste punten voor de klant en voor CCS en hoe vliegen we die aan. Na de lunch: Je checkt nog een paar tickets qua voortgang op het planboard, waarbij je de samenhang met de planning checkt. Vervolgens ga je naar de werksessie met het CCS projectmanagement guild. Hier werken jullie aan tickets om de CCS Prince2Agile projectmethodiek verder te verbeteren. Hierna heb je nog een afspraak met je collega van sales voor afstemming over een mogelijk vervolgproject bij de klant. Wie jij bent De ideale kandidaat beschikt over daadkracht, doorzettingsvermogen, enthousiasme en drive om projecten succesvol te leiden en verbeteringen door te voeren om te komen tot nog efficiëntere en klantgerichte projecten. Jij herkent jezelf in de volgende punten: · Je wordt blij van projectmanagement en blijft kalm bij verschuivende prioriteiten; · Je hebt bewezen ervaring met het succesvol uitvoeren van productsoftware-implementaties in een complexe, maar klantgerichte omgeving, binnen budget, planning en scope; · Je hebt ruime ervaring met diverse projectmanagement en delivery methodieken, bij voorkeur een Prince2-, Ipma of PMI of Agile / scrum certificaat; · Je vindt, net als wij, klanttevredenheid het uitgangspunt. The Opportunity Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone. Pioneer steerable generative models that can synthesize the full diversity of human speech from the codec latent representation, from casual conversation to highly emotional expression to complex multi-speaker scenarios with environmental noise and overlapping speech. Develop embedding systems that cleanly factorize the codec latent space into interpretable dimensions of speaker, content, style, environment, and channel effects -- enabling precise control over each aspect and the ability to massively amplify an existing seed dataset through “latent recombination”. Leverage latent recombination to generate synthetic audio data at previously impossible scales, unlocking joint model and data scaling paradigms for audio. Endeavor to train multimodal speech-to-speech systems that can 1) understand any human irrespective of their demographics, state, or environment and 2) produce empathic, human-like responses that achieve conversational or task-oriented objectives. Design model architectures, training schemes, and inference algorithms that are adapted for hardware at the bare metal enabling cost efficient training on billion-hour datasets and powering real-time inference for hundreds of millions of concurrent conversations. The Challenge We are seeking researchers who: See "unsolved" problems as opportunities to pioneer entirely new approaches Can identify the one critical experiment that will validate or kill an idea in days, not months Have the vision to scale successful proofs-of-concept 100x Are obsessed with using AI to automate and amplify your own impact If you find yourself energized rather than daunted by these expectations—if you're already thinking about five ideas to try while reading this—you might be the researcher we need. Below is a synthesis of how each paper highlights these qualities, with references illustrating why they matter for building robust, impactful deep learning models. 1. Statistical & Mathematical Foundations Mastery of Core Concepts Many papers, like Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models and Neural Discrete Representation Learning (VQ-VAE), reflect the importance of power-law analyses, derivation of novel losses, or adaptation of fundamental equations (e.g., in VQ-VAE's commitment loss or rectified flows in Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers). Such mathematical grounding clarifies why models converge or suffer collapse. Combining Existing Theories in Novel Ways Papers such as Moshi (combining text modeling, audio codecs, and hierarchical generative modeling) and Finite Scalar Quantization (FSQ's adaptation of classic scalar quantization to replace vector-quantized representations) show how reusing but reimagining known techniques can yield breakthroughs. Many references (e.g., the structured state-space duality in Transformers are SSMs) underscore how unifying previously separate research lines can reveal powerful algorithmic or theoretical insights. Logical Reasoning and Assumption Testing Across all papers—particularly in the problem statements of Whisper or Rectified Flow Transformers—the authors present assumptions (e.g., "scaling data leads to zero-shot robustness" or "straight-line noise injection improves sample efficiency") and systematically verify them with thorough empirical results. An ideal researcher similarly grounds new ideas in well-formed, testable hypotheses. 2. Algorithmic Innovation & Implementation Creative Solutions to Known Bottlenecks Each paper puts forth a unique algorithmic contribution—Rectified Flow Transformers redefines standard diffusion paths, FSQ proposes simpler scalar quantizations contrasted with VQ, phi-3 mini relies on curated data and blocksparse attention, and Mamba-2 merges SSM speed with attention concepts. Turning Theory into Practice Whether it's the direct preference optimization (DPO) for alignment in phi-3 or the residual vector quantization in SoundStream, these works show that bridging design insights with implementable prototypes is essential. Clear Impact Through Prototypes & Open-Source Many references (Whisper, neural discrete representation learning, Mamba-2) highlight releasing code or pretrained models, enabling the broader community to replicate and build upon new methods. This premise of collaboration fosters faster progress. 3. Data-Driven & Scalable Systems Emphasis on Large-Scale Data and Efficient Pipelines Papers such as Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision (Whisper) and BASE TTS demonstrate that collecting and processing hundreds of thousands of hours of real-world audio can unlock new capabilities in zero-shot or low-resource domains. Meanwhile, phi-3 Technical Report shows that filtering and curating data at scale (e.g., "data optimal regime") can yield high performance even in smaller models. Strategic Use of Data for Staged Training A recurring strategy is to vary sources of data or the order of tasks. Whisper trains on multilingual tasks, BASE TTS uses subsets/stages for pretraining on speech tokens, and phi-3 deploys multiple training phases (web data, then synthetic data). This systematic approach to data underscores how an ideal researcher designs training curricula and data filtering protocols for maximum performance. 4. Hardware & Systems Understanding Efficient Implementations at Scale Many works illustrate how researchers tune architectures for modern accelerators: the In-Datacenter TPU paper exemplifies domain-specific hardware design for dense matrix multiplications, while phi-3 leverages blocksparse attention and custom Triton kernels to run advanced LLMs on resource-limited devices. Real-Time & On-Device Constraints SoundStream shows how to compress audio in real time on a smartphone CPU, demonstrating that knowledge of hardware constraints (latency, limited memory) drives design choices. Similarly, Moshi's low-latency streaming TTS and phi-3-mini's phone-based inference highlight that an ideal researcher must adapt algorithms to resource limits while maintaining robustness. Architectural & Optimization Details Papers like Mamba-2 in Transformers are SSMs and the In-Datacenter TPU work show how exploiting specialized matrix decomposition, custom memory hierarchies, or quantization approaches can lead to breakthroughs in speed or energy efficiency. 5. Rigorous Experimental Design Controlled Comparisons & Ablations Nearly all papers—Whisper, FSQ, Mamba-2, BASE TTS—use systematic ablations to isolate the impact of individual components (e.g., ablation on vector-quantization vs. scalar quantization in FSQ, or size of codebooks in VQ-VAEs). This approach reveals which design decisions truly matter. Multifold Evaluation Metrics From MUSHRA listening tests (SoundStream, BASE TTS) to FID in image synthesis (Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers, FSQ) to perplexity or zero-shot generalization in language (phi-3, Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models), the works demonstrate the value of comprehensive, carefully chosen metrics. Stress Tests & Edge Cases Whisper's out-of-distribution speech benchmarks, SoundStream's evaluation on speech + music, or Mamba-2's performance on multi-query associative recall demonstrate the importance of specialized challenge sets. Researchers who craft or adopt rigorous benchmarks and "red-team" their models (as in phi-3 safety alignment) are better prepared to address real-world complexities. Summary Overall, an ideal researcher in deep learning consistently demonstrates: A solid grounding in theoretical and statistical principles A talent for proposing and validating new algorithmic solutions The capacity to orchestrate data pipelines that scale and reflect real-world diversity Awareness of hardware constraints and system-level trade-offs for efficiency Thorough and transparent experimental practices These qualities surface across research on speech (Whisper, BASE TTS), language modeling (Scaling Laws, phi-3), specialized hardware (TPU, Transformers are SSMs), and new representation methods (VQ-VAE, FSQ, SoundStream). By balancing these attributes—rigorous math, innovative algorithms, large-scale data engineering, hardware-savvy optimizations, and reproducible experimentation—researchers can produce impactful, trustworthy advancements in foundational deep learning. Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone.


The Role

As a Member of the Research Staff, you will pioneer the development of Latent Space Models (LSMs), a new approach that aims to solve the fundamental data, scale, and cost challenges associated with building robust, contextualized voice AI. Your research will focus on solving one or more of the following problems:

  • Build next-generation neural audio codecs that achieve extreme, low bit-rate compression and high fidelity reconstruction across a world-scale corpus of general audio.

  • Pioneer steerable generative models that can synthesize the full diversity of human speech from the codec latent representation, from casual conversation to highly emotional expression to complex multi-speaker scenarios with environmental noise and overlapping speech.

  • Develop embedding systems that cleanly factorize the codec latent space into interpretable dimensions of speaker, content, style, environment, and channel effects -- enabling precise control over each aspect and the ability to massively amplify an existing seed dataset through “latent recombination”.

  • Leverage latent recombination to generate synthetic audio data at previously impossible scales, unlocking joint model and data scaling paradigms for audio.  Endeavor to train multimodal speech-to-speech systems that can 1) understand any human irrespective of their demographics, state, or environment and 2) produce empathic, human-like responses that achieve conversational or task-oriented objectives.   

  • Design model architectures, training schemes, and inference algorithms that are adapted for hardware at the bare metal enabling cost efficient training on billion-hour datasets and powering real-time inference for hundreds of millions of concurrent conversations.

The Challenge

We are seeking researchers who:

  • See "unsolved" problems as opportunities to pioneer entirely new approaches

  • Can identify the one critical experiment that will validate or kill an idea in days, not months

  • Have the vision to scale successful proofs-of-concept 100x

  • Are obsessed with using AI to automate and amplify your own impact

If you find yourself energized rather than daunted by these expectations—if you're already thinking about five ideas to try while reading this—you might be the researcher we need. This role demands obsession with the problems, creativity in approach, and relentless drive toward elegant, scalable solutions. The technical challenges are immense, but the potential impact is transformative.

  • Strong mathematical foundation in statistical learning theory, particularly in areas relevant to self-supervised and multimodal learning

  • Deep expertise in foundation model architectures, with an understanding of how to scale training across multiple modalities

  • Proven ability to bridge theory and practice—someone who can both derive novel mathematical formulations and implement them efficiently

  • Demonstrated ability to build data pipelines that can process and curate massive datasets while maintaining quality and diversity

  • Track record of designing controlled experiments that isolate the impact of architectural innovations and validate theoretical insights

  • Experience optimizing models for real-world deployment, including knowledge of hardware constraints and efficiency techniques

  • History of open-source contributions or research publications that have advanced the state of the art in speech/language AI


Ideal Researcher Profile

An ideal researcher, as evidenced by the recurring themes across these foundational papers, excels in five key areas: (1) Statistical & Mathematical Foundations, (2) Algorithmic Innovation & Implementation, (3) Data-Driven & Scalable Systems, (4) Hardware & Systems Understanding, and (5) Rigorous Experimental Design. Below is a synthesis of how each paper highlights these qualities, with references illustrating why they matter for building robust, impactful deep learning models.



1. Statistical & Mathematical Foundations

Mastery of Core Concepts

Many papers, like Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models and Neural Discrete Representation Learning (VQ-VAE), reflect the importance of power-law analyses, derivation of novel losses, or adaptation of fundamental equations (e.g., in VQ-VAE's commitment loss or rectified flows in Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers). Such mathematical grounding clarifies why models converge or suffer collapse.

Combining Existing Theories in Novel Ways

Papers such as Moshi (combining text modeling, audio codecs, and hierarchical generative modeling) and Finite Scalar Quantization (FSQ's adaptation of classic scalar quantization to replace vector-quantized representations) show how reusing but reimagining known techniques can yield breakthroughs. Many references (e.g., the structured state-space duality in Transformers are SSMs) underscore how unifying previously separate research lines can reveal powerful algorithmic or theoretical insights.

Logical Reasoning and Assumption Testing

Across all papers—particularly in the problem statements of Whisper or Rectified Flow Transformers—the authors present assumptions (e.g., "scaling data leads to zero-shot robustness" or "straight-line noise injection improves sample efficiency") and systematically verify them with thorough empirical results. An ideal researcher similarly grounds new ideas in well-formed, testable hypotheses.


2. Algorithmic Innovation & Implementation

Creative Solutions to Known Bottlenecks

Each paper puts forth a unique algorithmic contribution—Rectified Flow Transformers redefines standard diffusion paths, FSQ proposes simpler scalar quantizations contrasted with VQ, phi-3 mini relies on curated data and blocksparse attention, and Mamba-2 merges SSM speed with attention concepts.

Turning Theory into Practice

Whether it's the direct preference optimization (DPO) for alignment in phi-3 or the residual vector quantization in SoundStream, these works show that bridging design insights with implementable prototypes is essential.

Clear Impact Through Prototypes & Open-Source

Many references (Whisper, neural discrete representation learning, Mamba-2) highlight releasing code or pretrained models, enabling the broader community to replicate and build upon new methods. This premise of collaboration fosters faster progress.


3. Data-Driven & Scalable Systems

Emphasis on Large-Scale Data and Efficient Pipelines

Papers such as Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision (Whisper) and BASE TTS demonstrate that collecting and processing hundreds of thousands of hours of real-world audio can unlock new capabilities in zero-shot or low-resource domains. Meanwhile, phi-3 Technical Report shows that filtering and curating data at scale (e.g., "data optimal regime") can yield high performance even in smaller models.

Strategic Use of Data for Staged Training

A recurring strategy is to vary sources of data or the order of tasks. Whisper trains on multilingual tasks, BASE TTS uses subsets/stages for pretraining on speech tokens, and phi-3 deploys multiple training phases (web data, then synthetic data). This systematic approach to data underscores how an ideal researcher designs training curricula and data filtering protocols for maximum performance.


4. Hardware & Systems Understanding

Efficient Implementations at Scale

Many works illustrate how researchers tune architectures for modern accelerators: the In-Datacenter TPU paper exemplifies domain-specific hardware design for dense matrix multiplications, while phi-3 leverages blocksparse attention and custom Triton kernels to run advanced LLMs on resource-limited devices.

Real-Time & On-Device Constraints

SoundStream shows how to compress audio in real time on a smartphone CPU, demonstrating that knowledge of hardware constraints (latency, limited memory) drives design choices. Similarly, Moshi's low-latency streaming TTS and phi-3-mini's phone-based inference highlight that an ideal researcher must adapt algorithms to resource limits while maintaining robustness.

Architectural & Optimization Details

Papers like Mamba-2 in Transformers are SSMs and the In-Datacenter TPU work show how exploiting specialized matrix decomposition, custom memory hierarchies, or quantization approaches can lead to breakthroughs in speed or energy efficiency.


5. Rigorous Experimental Design

Controlled Comparisons & Ablations

Nearly all papers—Whisper, FSQ, Mamba-2, BASE TTS—use systematic ablations to isolate the impact of individual components (e.g., ablation on vector-quantization vs. scalar quantization in FSQ, or size of codebooks in VQ-VAEs). This approach reveals which design decisions truly matter.

Multifold Evaluation Metrics

From MUSHRA listening tests (SoundStream, BASE TTS) to FID in image synthesis (Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers, FSQ) to perplexity or zero-shot generalization in language (phi-3, Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models), the works demonstrate the value of comprehensive, carefully chosen metrics.

Stress Tests & Edge Cases

Whisper's out-of-distribution speech benchmarks, SoundStream's evaluation on speech + music, or Mamba-2's performance on multi-query associative recall demonstrate the importance of specialized challenge sets. Researchers who craft or adopt rigorous benchmarks and "red-team" their models (as in phi-3 safety alignment) are better prepared to address real-world complexities.



Summary

Overall, an ideal researcher in deep learning consistently demonstrates:

  • A solid grounding in theoretical and statistical principles

  • A talent for proposing and validating new algorithmic solutions

  • The capacity to orchestrate data pipelines that scale and reflect real-world diversity

  • Awareness of hardware constraints and system-level trade-offs for efficiency

By balancing these attributes—rigorous math, innovative algorithms, large-scale data engineering, hardware-savvy optimizations, and reproducible experimentation—researchers can produce impactful, trustworthy advancements in foundational deep learning.

description: Who We Are Catalyst Capital is a profitable, bootstrapped holding company building a diversified financial services group: education, publishing, software, wealth and tax planning tools, investment products and proprietary trading technology. You will set the strategy, build the program, and personally run the response when something goes wrong. The job is two halves. Half is the core of a CISO's role: incident response, identity and access, vendor risk, phishing defense, policy and audit readiness, and the judgment calls only a person can own. The other half is making security AI-driven: mapping our full surface and building agentic systems that test, monitor and audit it with near-total coverage, so security keeps pace as more of the company runs on AI. This is a player-coach role: about half hands-on, leading a small team of engineers. You report to Group leadership, brief the leadership team monthly, and are the person they trust to explain risk in plain language and make the call under pressure. What you will own Core security leadership (about half) Security strategy and program. Own the security strategy, roadmap and budget across Decentralized Masters, Legacy, Inflection Club, Sentinelis and future brands. Report posture, top risks and trends to leadership every month, with a risk register leadership can act on. Incident response. Own IR end to end: detection, triage, containment, eradication, recovery and the postmortem. Lead the room during a live incident and coordinate with legal counsel, forensics firms, insurers and regulators. Keep runbooks current and run tabletop exercises. Cloud and identity security. Own identity and access across the group: SSO, MFA, least-privilege roles, admin redundancy and short-lived credentials. Set the AWS security baseline. Third-party and vendor risk. Assess the security of every vendor and data provider we depend on, including their audits and attestations, and set the bar a vendor must clear before connecting to our systems or data. Platform and customer account security. Set the standards for login protection and account-takeover defense on our platforms, and work with the engineering teams that own each platform to build them in. Phishing and impersonation defense. Own email security, staff training and phishing simulations. Run brand protection: find and take down fake domains and accounts impersonating our brands and leaders. Policy, compliance and trust. Write and enforce policies people actually follow. Prepare the company for SOC 2 or ISO 27001 with Legal & Compliance. Own the public security and trust story, including the trust page on our products. Team leadership. Manage and develop our security engineers, decide what we build in-house versus outsource, and grow the team only where automation cannot do the job. Member scam awareness. Supply the security content behind scam-awareness messaging to members, working with Community, Support and Marketing. Legal approves the wording. AI-driven security (about half) Full attack-surface map. Build and maintain a living inventory of everything we run: internal apps, cloud, code repos, and every SaaS tool and integration (CRM, telephony, community, payments, data providers). Know what connects to what, who has access, and what is logged. Agentic security harness. Design and run AI-driven systems that approach 100% coverage: automated code and dependency review, continuous configuration and access audits, and vendor documentation review. Humans set direction and make the judgment calls; agents do the exhaustive work. AI-driven detection and logging. Own the security stack (SIEM, Rapid7; endpoint protection; email security; identity and device management), make sure every critical system sends usable logs, and use AI to triage alerts and hunt across them. Secure AI and vibe-coding standards. Set the rules for how teams build with AI: what can ship, what data AI tools may touch, and the review path before anything with customer data goes live. AI agent security. As more of the company runs on agents and automations, secure them: scoped credentials and tool permissions, prompt-injection defense, data exposure, and monitoring and guardrails for agents in production. Review high-risk agents before launch, including our own security agents. Scope This role protects our company, our platforms, our data and our brands. For members' personal wallets and accounts outside our platforms, our role is education: helping members recognize and avoid scams. Requirements What you will bring Must have 10+ years in security, including 3+ years leading a security function as CISO, Head of Security or equivalent at a company of 100+ people. Has led live-incident response, not just tabletop exercises, including briefing executives during the incident. Has built or rebuilt a security program from an early stage: strategy, policy, tooling, training and incident response. AI-native operator. Uses AI agents daily to do the work: writing detections, reviewing code and configs, reading vendor documentation, drafting policy. Can show us the harnesses, workflows or automations you have built, and knows where AI stops and human judgment has to take over. Deep, current knowledge of AI-specific risks: prompt injection, over-scoped agent permissions, credential and data exposure through AI tools, and insecure AI-generated code. Hands-on with cloud security (AWS preferred), identity and access management, SIEM, endpoint protection and email security. Writes code: scripts, tooling and automation, not only vendor UIs. Experience in crypto, fintech or another high-fraud industry, and deep knowledge of phishing, social engineering and impersonation attacks. Can read the fine print: thorough with documentation, contracts and vendor security terms, and documents everything so nothing slips through. Briefs executives in plain language, trains non-technical staff, and writes policy people follow. Player-coach: comfortable spending about half your time hands-on while leading a small, fully remote team across many time zones. Nice to have Has prepared a company for SOC 2 or ISO 27001. Before that, Clay led the product and design teams for Google Workspace.

What you'll do

  • Prospecting & lead generation: Identify and target potential customers through research, networking, and cold calling. Build new relationships with our enterprise customers and prospects to drive revenue, pipeline, and deployment capacity.

What you'll bring

  • 10+ years of experience in an enterprise customer-facing sales role, identifying and closing large accounts.

  • Strong communication skills: Exceptional verbal and written communication abilities. Professional fluency in Dutch and English.

  • Enterprise experience: Experience managing a $1M+ quota, and running end-to-end complex deals.

  • Analytical mindset: Ability to analyze market trends, identify opportunities, and make data-driven decisions.

  • Prospecting & lead generation: Proven track record of identifying and targeting potential enterprise clients through research, networking, and cold calling.

Even better...

  • Industry knowledge: Familiarity with the AI landscape, key players, and emerging trends.

Our values

  • Trust: We build trust with our customers with our accountability, empathy, quality, and responsiveness. We build trust in AI by making it more accessible, safe, and useful. We build trust with each other by showing up for each other professionally and personally, creating an environment that enables all of us to do our best work.

title: Stage Frontoffice
description: Wat ga je doen? Een goede eerste indruk maken én jezelf ontwikkelen in gastvrijheid en communicatie? Daar krijg je tijdens jouw meewerkstage bij de Frontoffice volop de kans voor. Je bent een van de eerste aanspreekpunten voor bezoekers en bellers en leert hoe je hen vriendelijk en professioneel helpt. Je ontvangt gasten bij de receptie, neemt de telefoon op en voert verschillende administratieve werkzaamheden uit. Zo doe je in de praktijk ervaring op met receptiewerk, telefonie, hospitality, communicatie en administratie. Omdat we internationaal werken, krijg je ook te maken met buitenlandse bezoekers en telefoongesprekken. Je hoeft natuurlijk nog geen perfecte Engelse gesprekken te voeren. Het belangrijkste is dat je het leuk vindt om Engels in de praktijk te gebruiken en hierin steeds beter te worden. Wanneer het rustiger is bij de Frontoffice, dan ondersteun je bij Travel. Je helpt bijvoorbeeld met de administratie rondom zakelijke reizen, het verwerken en controleren van reisgegevens en, waar mogelijk, het boeken van hotels en vluchten. Zo ontdek je niet alleen hoe de Frontoffice werkt, maar krijg je ook inzicht in het organiseren van zakelijke reizen. Concreet ga je je bezighouden met: Bezoekers ontvangen en leren hoe je zorgt voor een gastvrije en professionele ontvangst; De telefoon aannemen en bellers doorverbinden of verder helpen; Ervaring opdoen met Nederlandse én Engelse telefoongesprekken; Werken met administratieve werkzaamheden en systemen; Ondersteunen bij Travel, bijvoorbeeld bij het verwerken en controleren van reisgegevens; Waar mogelijk helpen bij het boeken van hotels en vluchten voor zakelijke reizen; Steeds zelfstandiger meedraaien in de dagelijkse werkzaamheden van de Frontoffice. Het belangrijkste resultaat van jouw stage? Dat je steeds zelfstandiger kunt meedraaien bij de Frontoffice en jezelf verder ontwikkelt in gastvrijheid, communicatie en administratie. Daarnaast krijg je inzicht in Travel en leer je hoe de organisatie van zakelijke reizen er in de praktijk aan toegaat. Wij vragen Een mbo-opleiding in de richting van administratie, hospitality, toerisme of vergelijkbaar. Je bent gastrvij en vindt het leuk om mensen te helpen; Je werkt nauwkeurig en bent georganiseerd; Je durft initiatief te nemen en bent leergierig; Wij bieden Een vergoeding: €600,- per maand; Reiskostenvergoeding: zodat jij geen onnodige kosten maakt; Apparatuur en materialen: bijvoorbeeld een laptop of software; Ervaren coach: goede begeleiding is belangrijk en dus krijg je een vaste coach om je te ondersteunen; Ruimte voor persoonlijke ontwikkeling. Over Voortman Wat in 1968 begon in een kippenschuur in Rijssen, is uitgegroeid tot wereldspeler in CNC-staalbewerkingsmachines. Met een team van meer dan 750 collega’s wereldwijd ontwikkelen en bouwen we niet alleen high-end machines, maar ook slimme software en service waarop klanten kunnen vertrouwen. Deze 3 krachtige bouwstenen maken ons Twentse, internationale familiebedrijf uniek. Find Jobs in Netherlands on Arbeitnow

title: Applied AI Engineer
description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for an Applied AI Engineer based in Netherlands. As an Applied AI Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in designing and building the next generation of intelligent, agentic systems. You will develop the core infrastructure that enables AI agents to manage context, use tools, coordinate tasks, and continuously improve their performance. Working at the intersection of advanced AI research and practical software engineering, you will transform complex operational workflows into reliable, scalable production solutions. You will establish robust evaluation, testing, and observability frameworks to ensure AI-powered systems deliver predictable and measurable results. You will also explore innovative ways to integrate coding agents and specialized subagents into software development processes. Collaborating closely with product and operational teams, you will identify high-impact automation opportunities and translate them into effective technical solutions. As an early core member of the engineering team, you will have significant influence over architectural decisions, technical standards, and the long-term AI strategy. Accountabilities In this role, you will design and implement the technical foundations of agentic systems while driving the adoption of AI-powered engineering workflows. Your responsibilities will include: Design and build essential components of agentic systems, including memory, context management, tool-calling capabilities, orchestration mechanisms, and feedback loops. Develop reusable AI infrastructure that enables new workflows to be introduced quickly, consistently, and with predictable reliability. Build comprehensive evaluation frameworks to measure agent performance, identify failure points, and understand the factors behind successful outcomes. Integrate testing, tracing, debugging, and evaluation into the software engineering lifecycle as fundamental practices. Develop systems and validation processes that allow agentic workflows to be thoroughly assessed before production deployment. Advance the use of large language models (LLMs) in software development by creating sophisticated AI-assisted engineering workflows. Build workflows where coding agents and specialized subagents can explore code repositories, implement changes, review architecture, validate conventions, run evaluations, and iterate with minimal human intervention. Actively use agentic engineering tools and workflows in daily development activities. Design architectures that enable specialized AI agents, tools, deterministic software, and human expertise to work together effectively. Determine when to use LLMs, traditional software solutions, human intervention, or coordinated multi-agent approaches to achieve the best outcomes. Collaborate with operational and product teams to understand existing processes, identify high-value automation opportunities, and transform them into reliable production systems. Establish scalable architectural patterns and engineering standards for agentic systems as the organization grows. Take ownership of technical decisions and contribute to the overall direction of the AI engineering function. Requirements The ideal candidate is a strong software engineer with hands-on experience building production-ready AI systems and the autonomy to solve complex technical challenges in a rapidly evolving environment. The following qualifications and skills are expected: Strong software engineering background, with proven experience independently delivering complex systems from initial concept through production deployment. Practical experience building and deploying AI or agentic systems that have operated in production environments. Demonstrated understanding of real-world AI engineering challenges, including reliability, latency, context management, failure modes, evaluation, and observability. Strong knowledge of agent architectures, tool use, structured outputs, context management, orchestration, evaluation frameworks, and feedback loops. Advanced practical experience with modern LLMs and the ability to build reliable workflows around probabilistic AI systems. Hands-on experience using coding agents and agentic development workflows as part of everyday software engineering. Ability to break down complex engineering tasks across multiple agents or specialized subagents and implement mechanisms for validating and improving their outputs. Strong architectural judgment and the ability to select the right combination of AI models, deterministic software, and human intervention for different challenges. Experience with TypeScript and Node.js, or strong experience developing AI systems in Python combined with the willingness and ability to work in a TypeScript-first environment. High level of autonomy, ownership, and confidence making technical decisions in ambiguous situations. Strong product mindset and the ability to connect engineering decisions with operational efficiency and business outcomes. Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with fluency in English. Startup mentality, including resilience, adaptability, initiative, and the ability to thrive in a fast-paced environment. Benefits Competitive Compensation: Annual salary ranging from €100,000 to €150,000. Remote Work: Opportunity to work remotely within Europe or the United Kingdom. Early-Team Influence: Join as an early core engineering team member with significant ownership over technical direction and architectural decisions. Technical Autonomy: Shape engineering standards, development practices, tooling, and the foundations of the organization's agentic AI infrastructure. Cutting-Edge Technology: Work extensively with advanced LLMs, autonomous agents, multi-agent architectures, and AI-powered software development workflows. Meaningful Impact: Build production systems that address real operational challenges and deliver measurable business value. Cross-functional Collaboration: Work closely with product and operational teams to identify opportunities and develop practical automation solutions. Professional Growth: Take on challenging engineering problems while helping establish the foundations of a growing AI-focused organization. Our system identifies the top-fitting candidates, and this shortlist is then shared directly with the hiring company. The final decision and next steps (interviews, assessments) are managed by their internal team.
